rules.naturalLanguage: Backup, restore and DR must have stated RPO and RTO.
rules.lambda: input1.text.ToLower().Contains("rpo") || input1.text.ToLower().Contains("rto") || input1.text.ToLower().Contains("recovery point") || input1.text.ToLower().Contains("recovery time")
rules.remediation: State explicit RPO and RTO targets and the test cadence for restore drills.
rules.sourceContent: AU-06.R1Provide test report for the following: Choose a series of <tasks> to perform in the applicationChoose a <timeframe> when these tasks will be performed Choose user A accessing the application and performing <tasks> within the application during <timeframe>.Instruct user A to generate <application errors>Choose user B not accessing the application during <timeframe> (purpose is to confirm assurance user did not access the application as for instance confirming a threat actor did not access the data)Q1: did user A access the application during <timeframe>? What was the time?Q2: did user B access the application during <timeframe>? Confirm level of assurance Q3: What were the <tasks> and time performed by user A during <timeframe> Q4: Did the application reported any error during the last 7 days? If so, what were the errors?

rules.naturalLanguage: Data protection clause must reference an industry security standard.
rules.remediation: Add to the {section.heading} clause: "Provider shall maintain security controls aligned with {meta.requiredStandard}."
rules.sourceContent: SA-08.R3If PROTECTED data is used in development environment(s):Provide approval from business owner and evidence PSPC Privacy (if there is personal data) has been informed. Confirm safeguards will be identical across the environments.

rules.naturalLanguage: Data at rest must be encrypted using customer-managed keys (CMK) or platform-managed keys with documented rotation.
rules.remediation: Specify the encryption algorithm and key management model (e.g., "AES-256 with customer-managed keys in Azure Key Vault").
rules.sourceContent: SC-28.R1Provide evidence data is encrypted at rest.Data at rest refers to system information storage when not actively processed (compute) or in-transit. Encryption of the data must be, at the minimum, at the Disk / Volume level.

rules.naturalLanguage: Data in transit must be protected by TLS 1.2 or higher.
rules.remediation: State the minimum TLS version explicitly (TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3).
